comments.author: @ljbrienza
comments.text:
Some pretty outdated information for a video posted yesterday. Tesla now has an estimated 415 Robotaxis in Austin versus 300+ for Waymo, operates from 6 AM to 2 AM (20 hours daily), and covers roughly 270 square miles versus Waymo’s 130–140.

Tesla also logged 438,000 autonomous miles in Austin in one recent week versus Waymo’s reported Q2 average of 406,000 per week.

But the biggest omission is economics. Tesla is targeting a Cybercab under $30K, with potentially much lower manufacturing and operating costs per mile thanks to its camera-based approach and manufacturing scale.

Waymo deserves credit, but ignoring Tesla’s rapid expansion, larger service area, mileage growth and potential cost advantage misses a huge part of the story. It’s not just who’s ahead today, but who can scale millions of Robotaxis profitably.

comments.author: @jscottyman
comments.text:
The playbook lies open bare and people refuse to look at it. 1) Aggressive market capture: A couple of companies with deep pockets enters an industry, and they can afford to provide their services way below cost for a long time in order to run the establishment out of business (subsidized vehicles, subsidized charging, division cross-financing). 2) Squeeze the customers: Once the duopoly (or monopoly) has been established, they can raise prices. The barriers to entry are enormous. 3) Squeeze the employees: not really a major deal in this instance, but the few people (ex-taxi drivers?) who have to connect charging cables and clean the cabs won't have a great time.

Point being, even though driverless cabs are cheaper to operate than regular cabs, the customers will enjoy NONE of the gain. The industry has shifted from being labor intensive to capital intensive and it now requires a commitment in the order of double digits (of billion $) to be a serious threat. And it doesn't help that the owner class donates billions to influence political opinion in every election which all but ensures that public transportation will never become a viable option. This path only leads to a worse outcome in the long run.
